---
title: "Chat_apples"
format: html
---

```{r}
## Load necessary packages
library(tidyverse)  ## Provides many useful functions
library(dplyr)      ## Data crunching functions
library(gt)         ## For creating tables

## Data input
data <- tibble(
  orchard = c("Traditional", "Experimental"),
  apples_collected = c(592, 623),
  time_hours = c(2, 2),
  rate = c(592 / 2, 623 / 2)
)

## Create a nicely formatted table with gt
table_title <- "Apple Harvesting Results: 2 Hour Calibration Test"
data_source <- paste0("Source: ", "Orchard Experiment", " (", Sys.Date(), ")")

table <- data %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = table_title
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = data_source
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    orchard = "Orchard Type",
    apples_collected = "Apples Collected",
    time_hours = "Time (Hours)",
    rate = "Rate"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(apples_collected, rate),
    decimals = 0
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(v_align = "top"),
    locations = cells_body()
  ) %>%
  opt_row_striping(row_striping = TRUE) %>%
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = everything()
  ) %>%
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Units: apples per hour",
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = "rate")
  )

## Print the table
table

```

```{r}
## Load necessary packages
library(tidyverse)  ## Provides many useful functions
library(ggplot2)    ## For creating plots

## Data input
data <- tibble(
  orchard = c("Traditional", "Experimental"),
  rate = c(592 / 2, 623 / 2)
)

## Create a bar chart
bar_chart <- ggplot(data, aes(x = orchard, y = rate, fill = orchard)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("cornsilk3", "cornsilk3")) + 
  labs(
    title = "Apple Harvesting Rate: 2 Hour Calibration Test",
    x = "Orchard Type",
    y = "Rate (apples per hour)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "darkslategray3"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

## Print the bar chart
print(bar_chart)

```
